topic.title_he: להתכונן לשינה: שגרת ערב ועוד כוס מים
topic.reason: ביקשת אצווה של כל האופציות על התכוננות לשינה. הנושא הקרוב ביותר בבנק הנושאים הוא ״עוד כוס מים לפני השינה״ (bedtime-stalling), והוא לא היה בשימוש ב-14 החבילות האחרונות. אין כאן עובדת לוח שנה. החבילה נכתבה לתיקיית 12.10 ולא ל-11.10: ב-11.10 מחכה החבילה על כיתה א׳, והריצה של 22:00 הערב הייתה קוברת את האצווה הזאת. שימו לב: דף ה-AAP על ״7 טיפים״ כתוב לפעוטות ואנחנו מיישמים אותו על גילאי 3 עד 5, ודף ה-NHS עבר את תאריך הבדיקה הבאה שלו (מרץ 2026).

voice.note: קול ברירת מחדל: 3 מתוך 15 דוגמאות מאושרות. נכתב לפי קול ברירת המחדל המתועד ולפי העריכות של ירין מ-8.10 ו-9.10 (קיצור, בלי ״הרבה פעמים״ בקול של הילד, מירכאות סביב משפט שאומרים, ״לחזק אותה בעזרת סיפור״). עדיין לא מכויל לירין.

sources.title: Toddler Won't Go to Sleep? 7 Tips to Help End Bedtime Battles
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics); the page shows Last Updated 10/8/2026
sources.quote: Make bedtime the same time every night. ... This helps your child know what to expect and helps them establish healthy sleep patterns. ... Set up a quiet routine before bedtime ... Use this time to read them a story, put on quiet music, or give them a bath. ... It may be tempting to play with your child before bed. However, active play may make your child too excited to sleep. ... Take care of child's needs before bedtime so they don't use them as reasons to avoid going to sleep. They may want a drink of water, a light left on, or the door left slightly open. ... Let your child take a favorite thing to bed each night. ... Children this age often resist going to sleep
sources.supports: Same bedtime every night; a quiet pre-bed routine (story, quiet music, bath); active play can overexcite before sleep; take care of needs such as a drink of water before bedtime so they are not used as reasons to delay; a favourite thing to take to bed; young children often resist sleep. The page is written for toddlers; we apply it to ages 3 to 5 as a related situation.

sources.title: Sleep and young children
sources.publisher: NHS (nhs.uk); the page shows last reviewed 31 March 2023 and next review due 31 March 2026, a date that has passed, so it may have been updated since
sources.quote: calming, predictable bedtime routine that happens at the same time ... Start a "winding down" bedtime routine around 30 minutes before the time that your child usually falls asleep. ... For example, read only 1 story, then tuck your child in and say goodnight. ... If your child gets up, keep taking them back to bed again with as little fuss as possible. ... Do not let your child look at laptops, tablets or phones in the 30 to 60 minutes before bed ... If your child complains that they're hungry at night, try giving them a bowl of cereal and milk before bed
sources.supports: A calming predictable routine at the same time; start winding down about 30 minutes before usual sleep time; limit bedtime interaction (one story, then tuck in and say goodnight); take a child who gets up back to bed with little fuss; no laptops, tablets or phones 30 to 60 minutes before bed; a bowl of cereal and milk if hungry. Written for under 5s.

sources.title: Brush, Book, Bed: How to Structure Your Child's Nighttime Routine
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics); the page shows Last Updated 2/2/2024
sources.quote: Each night, help your children to brush their teeth. ... Read a favorite book (or two)! ... Get to bed at a regular time each night. ... Having a predictable nighttime routine can help your child understand and learn to expect what comes next. ... Do not wait for your child to start rubbing their eyes or yawning ... that's probably too late. Putting your child to bed even 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference ... Spending some time, even just 15 minutes each day, to read aloud together will help improve your child's language development and social-emotional skills.
sources.supports: Teeth, book, bed at a regular time; a predictable routine helps a child learn what comes next; yawning or rubbing eyes means it is probably too late; going to bed 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference; reading aloud together supports language and social-emotional skills.

sources.title: Brush, Book, Bed: How to Structure Your Child's Nighttime Routine
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics); the page shows Last Updated 2/2/2024
sources.quote: Each night, help your children to brush their teeth. ... Read a favorite book (or two)! ... Get to bed at a regular time each night. ... Having a predictable nighttime routine can help your child understand and learn to expect what comes next. ... Do not wait for your child to start rubbing their eyes or yawning ... that's probably too late. Putting your child to bed even 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference ... Spending some time, even just 15 minutes each day, to read aloud together will help improve your child's language development and social-emotional skills.
sources.supports: Teeth, book, bed at a regular time; a predictable routine helps a child learn what comes next; yawning or rubbing eyes means it is probably too late; going to bed 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference; reading aloud together supports language and social-emotional skills.

sources.title: Toddler Won't Go to Sleep? 7 Tips to Help End Bedtime Battles
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics); the page shows Last Updated 10/8/2026
sources.quote: Make bedtime the same time every night. ... This helps your child know what to expect and helps them establish healthy sleep patterns. ... Set up a quiet routine before bedtime ... Use this time to read them a story, put on quiet music, or give them a bath. ... It may be tempting to play with your child before bed. However, active play may make your child too excited to sleep. ... Take care of child's needs before bedtime so they don't use them as reasons to avoid going to sleep. They may want a drink of water, a light left on, or the door left slightly open. ... Let your child take a favorite thing to bed each night. ... Children this age often resist going to sleep
sources.supports: Same bedtime every night; a quiet pre-bed routine (story, quiet music, bath); active play can overexcite before sleep; take care of needs such as a drink of water before bedtime so they are not used as reasons to delay; a favourite thing to take to bed; young children often resist sleep. The page is written for toddlers; we apply it to ages 3 to 5 as a related situation.

sources.title: Sleep and young children
sources.publisher: NHS (nhs.uk); the page shows last reviewed 31 March 2023 and next review due 31 March 2026, a date that has passed, so it may have been updated since
sources.quote: calming, predictable bedtime routine that happens at the same time ... Start a "winding down" bedtime routine around 30 minutes before the time that your child usually falls asleep. ... For example, read only 1 story, then tuck your child in and say goodnight. ... If your child gets up, keep taking them back to bed again with as little fuss as possible. ... Do not let your child look at laptops, tablets or phones in the 30 to 60 minutes before bed ... If your child complains that they're hungry at night, try giving them a bowl of cereal and milk before bed
sources.supports: A calming predictable routine at the same time; start winding down about 30 minutes before usual sleep time; limit bedtime interaction (one story, then tuck in and say goodnight); take a child who gets up back to bed with little fuss; no laptops, tablets or phones 30 to 60 minutes before bed; a bowl of cereal and milk if hungry. Written for under 5s.

sources.title: Sleep and young children
sources.publisher: NHS (nhs.uk); the page shows last reviewed 31 March 2023 and next review due 31 March 2026, a date that has passed, so it may have been updated since
sources.quote: calming, predictable bedtime routine that happens at the same time ... Start a "winding down" bedtime routine around 30 minutes before the time that your child usually falls asleep. ... For example, read only 1 story, then tuck your child in and say goodnight. ... If your child gets up, keep taking them back to bed again with as little fuss as possible. ... Do not let your child look at laptops, tablets or phones in the 30 to 60 minutes before bed ... If your child complains that they're hungry at night, try giving them a bowl of cereal and milk before bed
sources.supports: A calming predictable routine at the same time; start winding down about 30 minutes before usual sleep time; limit bedtime interaction (one story, then tuck in and say goodnight); take a child who gets up back to bed with little fuss; no laptops, tablets or phones 30 to 60 minutes before bed; a bowl of cereal and milk if hungry. Written for under 5s.

sources.title: Toddler Won't Go to Sleep? 7 Tips to Help End Bedtime Battles
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics); the page shows Last Updated 10/8/2026
sources.quote: Make bedtime the same time every night. ... This helps your child know what to expect and helps them establish healthy sleep patterns. ... Set up a quiet routine before bedtime ... Use this time to read them a story, put on quiet music, or give them a bath. ... It may be tempting to play with your child before bed. However, active play may make your child too excited to sleep. ... Take care of child's needs before bedtime so they don't use them as reasons to avoid going to sleep. They may want a drink of water, a light left on, or the door left slightly open. ... Let your child take a favorite thing to bed each night. ... Children this age often resist going to sleep
sources.supports: Same bedtime every night; a quiet pre-bed routine (story, quiet music, bath); active play can overexcite before sleep; take care of needs such as a drink of water before bedtime so they are not used as reasons to delay; a favourite thing to take to bed; young children often resist sleep. The page is written for toddlers; we apply it to ages 3 to 5 as a related situation.

sources.title: Brush, Book, Bed: How to Structure Your Child's Nighttime Routine
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics); the page shows Last Updated 2/2/2024
sources.quote: Each night, help your children to brush their teeth. ... Read a favorite book (or two)! ... Get to bed at a regular time each night. ... Having a predictable nighttime routine can help your child understand and learn to expect what comes next. ... Do not wait for your child to start rubbing their eyes or yawning ... that's probably too late. Putting your child to bed even 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference ... Spending some time, even just 15 minutes each day, to read aloud together will help improve your child's language development and social-emotional skills.
sources.supports: Teeth, book, bed at a regular time; a predictable routine helps a child learn what comes next; yawning or rubbing eyes means it is probably too late; going to bed 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference; reading aloud together supports language and social-emotional skills.
